contracts: tasks__check_item(task_id, index, done=True) auto-activates task_id for the current scope as a direct side effect when done=True -- not via the _tool(hook=...) mechanism, but inline in the tool body via _auto_activate_on_checklist_progress. As of task:f5ace343 this is unconditional: active status is a single ephemeral pointer, not a stack, so checking an item on any task simply replaces whatever was active (no more lifecycle.check_active_switch confirm gate, no more 'active_task_notice' when a different task was active -- that gate and the check_active_switch function it called were both removed along with the stack). set_active is a no-op when task_id is already active. done=False (unchecking) never activates anything.

tasks__set_active/tasks__active/tasks__clear_active response shapes carry no stack_depth or stack list (task:f5ace343) -- {'ok', 'active', 'scope'} / {'active', 'scope'} / {'ok', 'active': null, 'scope'} respectively, mirroring the single in-memory pointer store.set_active/get_active/clear_active now hold.
tasks__create clears any active task for its scope on the way out (task:74bf3542) -- starting a new task is a clean break from whatever was active before it, not an implicit continuation.

tasks__set_active/tasks__clear_active best-effort POST {workspace, task_id, title} to claude-hooks' running server via _push_active_task (task:6906557f) -- a courtesy push, not a dependency; every failure mode (connection refused, timeout, DNS, non-2xx) is swallowed and logged at debug, and the tool's own return value/error semantics are unaffected either way.
active-task-pointer-lifecycle.description: Pulled out of [[mcp-portable-interface]]. The active-task pointer is a single in-memory value per scope (task:f5ace343) -- not a stack, not persisted, gone on server restart. tasks__check_item auto-activates unconditionally on done=True, tasks__create clears whatever was active on the way out, and claude-hooks receives a best-effort courtesy push whose failure never affects a tool's own result.
invariants: _push_active_task reads CLAUDE_HOOKS_URL from os.environ on every call rather than caching it at import time, specifically so tests can redirect it via monkeypatch.setenv without needing to reload the module -- a module-level constant computed once at import would not observe a later monkeypatch.setenv (task:6906557f).

Active status is now exactly as long-lived as the pass that sets it (task:f5ace343) -- task-grooming and task-introspection skills activate/deactivate at their own pass boundaries rather than relying on any persistence layer.
active-task-pointer-lifecycle.name: active-task-pointer-lifecycle

contracts: introspection_nudge(report, task_id, conn) -> str | None; fires only when the report has an unpromoted lesson (via _lesson_texts, covering both new_knowledge and legacy surprises[].lesson shapes) AND the task has never cited any memory (via _cited_in_memory).

drift_reflection_nudge(active_task_id, active_task_title='', active_task_phase='', active_task_next_item='', call_count=None, active_task_completed_items=None) -> str | None; fires every _DRIFT_NUDGE_INTERVAL calls when call_count is supplied, else every call. Invoked from taskfw/drift_hook.py's PostToolUse hook, which resolves scope itself via TaskStore before calling; active_task_next_item and active_task_completed_items are derived fresh from task.resolution by the caller each time, never stored.
finish_nudge(task) -> str | None; fires only when task.introspection is empty, at tasks__finish.
finish_reminder_nudge(task) -> str | None; fires when is_implemented(task) is True AND task.status == 'open', at tasks__check_item/tasks__update, before finish is called.
stale_memory_nudge(memory: dict) -> str | None; fires when memory['standing'] is 'disputed' or 'contradicted' (never 'superseded', already flagged by definition), wired onto task_memory__link.
ungroomed_progress_nudge(task) -> str | None; fires when task.progress has at least one checked item AND task.grooming is empty, at tasks__check_item/tasks__update.
loop_debt_nudge(skipped: int, tasks_examined: int) -> str | None; fires only when skipped > 0, wired onto tasks__set_active via mcp_server._loop_debt_hook.

task_debt_nudge(task_id: str, ungraded: int) -> str | None; fires only when ungraded > 0, companion to loop_debt_nudge — that one is about the loop across recent finished tasks, this one about the specific task just made active.
advisory-nudge-policies.description: The individual nudge functions — each a Callable[[...]] -> str | None encoding one advisory firing condition, wired onto a specific MCP tool via [[nudge-dispatch-chassis]]'s tool_called/combine/apply_nudge, and reading task state through [[task-phase-derivation]] where relevant. A nudge never blocks a write or changes what gets stored; it only surfaces something true about the result that would otherwise be silent. Extracted from the flat taskfw/dispatcher.py into taskfw/dispatcher/nudges.py; re-exported unchanged from taskfw/dispatcher/__init__.py.
invariants: loop_debt_nudge and task_debt_nudge surface at tasks__set_active, not inside tasks__context's bundle and not on tasks__create — set_active is the earlier of the two documented lifecycle entry points, and tasks__context is already budget-constrained around per-task relevance.

Both loop_debt_nudge and task_debt_nudge derive their counts from taskfw.accuracy._task_grading/loop_debt — the same classification tasks__grooming_accuracy itself uses — so none of the three can disagree about what counts as ungraded or skipped.
loop_debt_nudge/task_debt_nudge are not throttled by a call counter (unlike drift_reflection_nudge) — tasks__set_active is called far less often per session than every MCP tool call.

loop_debt is computed over the whole shared task store, not scoped to the calling project — Task has no project/scope field, so a debt count surfaced while working in one repo can be driven by unrelated finished tasks in another (task:07f9270c's grooming, a known, accepted risk).

finish_reminder_nudge closes a distinct gap from finish_nudge: finish_nudge fires AFTER tasks__finish when introspection is missing; finish_reminder_nudge fires on tasks__check_item/tasks__update BEFORE finish, when the checklist is complete but finish was never called (task:a6fb9f45 sat open at 4/4 until an unrelated review pass caught it).
stale_memory_nudge never calls supersede()/forget() itself — advisory only, consistent with task-introspection's 'never unilaterally delete stale memories' rule.

finish_reminder_nudge, stale_memory_nudge, and ungroomed_progress_nudge are all stateless by design (unlike drift_reflection_nudge's throttled counter): each checks current state on every qualifying call rather than firing once and remembering it fired, because check_item/update/link are infrequent enough that re-firing costs little.

ungroomed_progress_nudge and finish_nudge call task-phase-derivation's is_groomed/is_introspected (task:5a5fde0d) rather than testing task.grooming/task.introspection directly, so they and task_phase() (see [[task-phase-derivation]]) can never disagree about what those words mean.

drift_reflection_nudge is an awareness nudge, not a detection mechanism: it has no view into what happened during the call it's attached to, so it cannot tell drift from on-task work — it only puts the task label back in front of the caller on every qualifying call. The %N==0 throttle decision lives here in taskfw (call_count is supplied data from claude-hooks' own per-session counter via drift_hook.py's stdin payload); claude-hooks supplies data, not policy.

nudges.py imports is_groomed, is_implemented, and is_introspected from phase.py (one-directional, task:5a5fde0d) and imports nothing from chassis.py — every nudge here is a plain function returning str | None, wiring onto tool_called/apply_nudge happens only at the mcp_server.py call site, not inside this module.
advisory-nudge-policies.name: advisory-nudge-policies

contracts: A commit referencing an unknown task id is counted in unknown_tasks rather than raising.
backfill-recovers-without-the-original-c.description: Pins that taskfw.backfill.backfill never depends on tasks__add_commit having been called — it recovers task-commit links purely by scanning real git log output for task:<id> references, is idempotent (a second run reports already_linked rather than re-linking), and dry_run never writes to the store.
invariants: backfill() must produce identical results whether or not any tasks__add_commit call ever happened for a given commit.
dry_run=True must never call store.add_commit.
backfill-recovers-without-the-original-c.name: backfill-recovers-without-the-original-call

claude-hooks-push-best-effort-not-requir.description: Pins tasks__set_active/clear_active's push to claude-hooks' /set-active-taskid endpoint as strictly best-effort: it must post the workspace, task id, and title (empty strings on clear) with a bounded timeout, but any network failure -- connection refused, an unreachable CLAUDE_HOOKS_URL, or a raised exception from urlopen -- must never surface as a tool failure or block the local state change from succeeding.
invariants: tasks__set_active(id) POSTs {workspace, task_id, title} to CLAUDE_HOOKS_URL + '/set-active-taskid' with timeout=m._PUSH_TIMEOUT_S.
tasks__clear_active() POSTs the same shape with task_id and title as empty strings.
Any exception raised by urlopen (ConnectionRefusedError or otherwise) is swallowed -- the tool result still reports ok=True and the local active-task state still updates.
This holds against both a mocked urlopen and the real urllib path against a genuinely unreachable port, so the real network exception class is proven caught, not just a mock's stand-in.
claude-hooks-push-best-effort-not-requir.name: claude-hooks-push-best-effort-not-required

contracts: backfill(repo, since=None, dry_run=False) -> {scanned, linked, already_linked, unknown_tasks, dry_run}
git_log(repo, since) -> [(sha, message)], empty when the path is not a git repo
extract_task_ids(text) -> every task:<id> reference, de-duplicated, order preserved
commit-backfill-recovery.description: Rebuilds commit-to-task links by scanning git history for task:<id> references. There is no automatic capture: a commit is linked by an explicit tasks__add_commit call, made by the commit skill after a successful commit, and nothing enforces that call happens. This exists because that gap is invisible by construction: a task with no commits looks identical to one whose commits were never linked.
invariants: Idempotent — add_commit is a no-op for an already-recorded pair, so repeated runs are safe
A non-git directory is not an error, it is zero commits scanned
Git history is the durable record; the commit map is a cache over it, and this rebuilds the cache from scratch
Never depends on tasks__add_commit having been called — re-derives every link straight from git log
commit-backfill-recovery.name: commit-backfill-recovery

contracts: source_modules() is the single definition of what 'coverage' means; TestCoverage's tests must never diverge on scope.
concept-store-coverage-enforced-by-test.description: Whether the concept store stays refreshed after each task is answered structurally rather than by discipline: this test file fails the suite the moment a scanned source module has no concept, or a concept describes a module that no longer exists, or an evidence citation points at a missing file. source_modules() defines the scanned scope.
invariants: Every non-trivial *.py file under the scanned scope must have at least one concept whose module field matches it exactly.
No concept's module or evidence file path may reference a deleted file.
Every concept must state at least one invariant and a non-stub description (>80 chars) — a concept with neither is a summary, not architectural knowledge.
concept-store-coverage-enforced-by-test.name: concept-store-coverage-enforced-by-test

contracts: ConceptStore(repo) loads on construction; missing file is empty, not an error
list(module="") / get(name) / modules() / search(query) / uncovered(modules) are reads
upsert(concept) MERGES and returns the merged concept; delete(name) -> bool
concept__* MCP tools take repo explicitly, with no default
concept__get returns {found: bool, concept: {...}} on both branches — never the concept's fields flattened onto the response
concept-store-name-keyed-map.description: JSON-backed store of architectural concepts for a repo, plus the concept__* MCP tools over it. Makes the framework self-contained: before this, task-framework had a concept store it could not read without another project running its server. The on-disk format is deliberately identical to the established one so a store stays readable by either implementation and neither project owns the format. As of task:756c14db, this is the SOLE concept__* MCP surface for JSON-format concept stores — claude-hooks' own duplicate (src/tools/concept.py) was removed once concept__get's response shape was corrected here to match what claude-hooks' skills already depended on by bare tool name.
invariants: concepts is a NAME-KEYED MAP on disk, never a list — a list is rejected at load with a message naming the problem rather than failing later with AttributeError
Every accessor iterates self._concepts, never the loaded file: calling .values()/.items() on the top level yields "concepts" and "meta" as if they were concepts
A store without the {concepts, meta} wrapper is treated as the bare map, detected by absence of the key rather than by inspecting contents
upsert merges rather than overwrites, so updating one field cannot silently drop invariants the caller did not mention; an explicit empty list still clears
created_at survives an update; last_validated is restamped on every upsert
repo is always an explicit argument — a store is never tied to whichever server is running

save() writes with ensure_ascii=False — without it, every em-dash and non-ASCII character in an untouched concept gets re-escaped on any single-entry write, producing a whole-file diff for a one-entry change

concept__get's found:True branch nests under concept: {...} rather than flattening fields onto the response, so "found" cannot collide with a real field name and a caller does not need to know which implementation answered the call

upsert merges at the LIST-ENTRY level, not just the field level: a payload naming contracts/invariants/evidence unions those entries with what's already stored (dedup by exact match) rather than replacing the list outright, so a caller updating one entry cannot silently drop the others it did not mention (task:706a498f, fixing a prior bug where any mention of the field replaced the whole list) — an explicit empty list still clears.
concept-store-name-keyed-map.name: concept-store-name-keyed-map

contracts: concept__get always returns {found, concept} on both branches, never flattening concept fields onto the top-level result.
concept-store-self-contained-no-external.description: Pins that task-framework reads its own concept_store/concepts.json without depending on another project's MCP server, and that ConceptStore.upsert performs field-level merge semantics (list fields union rather than replace, an explicit empty list still clears, related is capped at 3 across merges, not just per payload) rather than a blind overwrite.
invariants: A payload naming only some list-field entries must not drop entries it didn't mention.
related merges are capped at 3 total across all merges, so a payload that looks valid alone can still be rejected if the union overflows.
Non-ASCII text is written to disk literally, never \uXXXX-escaped, since ensure_ascii=True would rewrite every untouched entry's em-dashes on any single-entry write.
concept-store-self-contained-no-external.name: concept-store-self-contained-no-external-server

connection-pragma-enforcement-and-fk-int.description: Pins the connection-level guarantees taskfw.db.connect.connect() must establish on every handle: WAL journaling, a positive busy_timeout, and enforced foreign keys, plus the constraint layer's idempotent-insert behavior for edges and commit captures via natural-key uniqueness.
invariants: Every connection from connect() has journal_mode=wal, busy_timeout > 0, and foreign_keys=1.
Inserting a task_event referencing a nonexistent task_id raises sqlite3.IntegrityError rather than silently orphaning the row.
Re-inserting an identical task_edge or task_commit natural key raises sqlite3.IntegrityError, giving callers idempotency for free rather than requiring an application-level check-then-insert.
connection-pragma-enforcement-and-fk-int.name: connection-pragma-enforcement-and-fk-integrity-tested

contracts: connect(path=None) -> sqlite3.Connection with row_factory=Row, migrated on first use per path
transaction(conn) commits on success and rolls back on any exception
connection-pragmas-single-point.description: connect() is the only place connection pragmas are set, and runs migrations once per database path. WAL, busy_timeout, and foreign_keys are applied here rather than left to callers because several processes write the same file concurrently.
invariants: WAL, busy_timeout, and foreign_keys are set for every connection, never by a caller
WAL is skipped for :memory:, where it does not apply
Migration runs at most once per path per process
connection-pragmas-single-point.name: connection-pragmas-single-point

contracts: build_context's returned top-level keys on a non-truncating bundle exactly match _BUNDLE_SKELETON's keys.
context-bundle-trim-behavior-pinned.description: Pins tasks__context's full contract beyond what build_context's own docstring states: section presence and order, that trimming always reports what it dropped (truncated, grooming_truncated, edges_truncated) so an omitted section never looks identical to an absent one, and the relevance floor that keeps related/lessons from filling with the best-available-however-weak match.
invariants: A section dropped for budget must always be named in truncated, never silently emptied.
grooming trims field-by-field (least useful first) before falling back to a whole-section drop, unlike every other section.
related_candidates and lessons_for must both reject a candidate with zero meaningful (4+ letter, non-numeric) word overlap with the task's query terms.
context-bundle-trim-behavior-pinned.name: context-bundle-trim-behavior-pinned

db-migration-destructive-sql-impossible-.description: Enforces the AdditiveOnlyMigration requirement structurally rather than by convention: taskfw.db.schema.migrate() must be observably incapable of emitting DROP, DELETE, or a non-additive ALTER TABLE, verified via sqlite3's set_trace_callback so every statement the connection actually executes is inspected, not just the statements the test author expected.
invariants: migrate() never emits a statement containing DROP or DELETE.
Every ALTER TABLE statement migrate() emits contains ADD COLUMN.
An orphaned/unknown column is reported in the migration result but left in the schema, never dropped.
migrate() is idempotent: a second call against an already-migrated connection creates nothing and adds nothing.
db-migration-destructive-sql-impossible-.name: db-migration-destructive-sql-impossible-by-test

dispatcher-nudge-firing-conditions-pinne.description: Pins the exact firing/silencing conditions for each advisory nudge in taskfw.dispatcher: introspection_nudge only counts new_knowledge and legacy surprises-with-lesson fields (never bare surprises or missed_surprises), and goes permanently silent once any memory has been cited from the task, regardless of report shape. Several nudges (ungroomed_progress_nudge, stale_memory_nudge on contradicted/disputed) are deliberately stateless and re-fire on every call rather than tracking a shown-once flag.
invariants: introspection_nudge fires only when new_knowledge or surprises[].lesson is present, never on missed_surprises or lesson-less surprises.
introspection_nudge returns None permanently once the task has any cited memory (learned_from), independent of the report passed in.
stale_memory_nudge fires only on contradicted/disputed standing, never on unverified, confirmed, or superseded.
ungroomed_progress_nudge and finish_reminder_nudge re-fire on every call while their condition still holds -- they hold no internal counter.
dispatcher-nudge-firing-conditions-pinne.name: dispatcher-nudge-firing-conditions-pinned

dispatcher-submodule-reexport-guard.description: Guards the risk flagged when dispatcher.py was split into chassis/phase/nudges submodules: a name defined in one of those submodules but forgotten from taskfw.dispatcher.__init__'s __all__ becomes reachable via the submodule but invisible through the public taskfw.dispatcher import, a silent two-tier API that only a structural test would notice.
invariants: Every public (non-underscore-prefixed) name actually defined in chassis, phase, or nudges must appear in taskfw.dispatcher.__all__.
Membership is checked by comparing inspect.getmodule(obj) to the defining submodule, so re-imported names from elsewhere don't produce false positives.
dispatcher-submodule-reexport-guard.name: dispatcher-submodule-reexport-guard

drift-hook-call-count-plumbing-pinned.description: Pins the stdin-to-gating plumbing of taskfw/drift_hook.py separately from the throttling logic itself (which belongs to dispatcher.drift_reflection_nudge and is tested in test_dispatcher.py). build_nudge must pass call_count through to the dispatcher unchanged, and main() must fail open -- treating a missing or non-int _taskfw_drift_call_count field, or fully malformed stdin JSON, as no counter at all rather than erroring.
invariants: build_nudge(store, scope, call_count) forwards call_count to dispatcher.drift_reflection_nudge without transformation.
A missing '_taskfw_drift_call_count' key, a non-int value for it, or unparseable stdin JSON must all be treated as call_count=None (fires every call) and main() must still return 0, never raise.
drift-hook-call-count-plumbing-pinned.name: drift-hook-call-count-plumbing-pinned

contracts: build_nudge(store, scope, call_count) returns None if no active task for scope, else dispatcher.drift_reflection_nudge(...)'s result, passing call_count through unchanged and also passing next_open_item(active_task) and completed_items(active_task) (task:1d23eb67) computed fresh from the active task's resolution on every call
main() reads JSON from stdin; a malformed/empty payload is treated as {} rather than raising
main() reads payload.get('_taskfw_drift_call_count'); a missing or non-int value is normalized to None, which makes drift_reflection_nudge fire on every call (pre-task:1c8f0815 behavior)
main() fails open on any exception from build_nudge (log.exception, return 0) — a crashing hook must never block the tool call it's attached to
main() emits nothing on stdout (not even an empty JSON object) when there's no nudge — PostToolUse reads silence as 'nothing to add'
_scope() mirrors mcp_server._scope(): TASKFW_SCOPE env var if set, else os.getcwd()
drift-hook-posttooluse-entrypoint.description: A standalone PostToolUse hook Claude Code (via claude-hooks' dispatcher.py) invokes as a fresh subprocess on every tool call in a session — not just taskfw's own MCP tools. Reads a JSON hook payload from stdin, looks up the active task for the calling scope via TaskStore, and if one exists, calls dispatcher.drift_reflection_nudge to build an awareness-nudge string, writing it back as PostToolUse hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext on stdout. Genuinely stateless: since it's a fresh subprocess per call, it cannot hold a cross-call counter itself (task:8be768df); claude-hooks' own dispatcher.py counts PostToolUse calls and passes the raw count in via stdin as "_taskfw_drift_call_count", forwarded unchanged. This module never decides whether to nudge or what to include — it only wires the stdin payload, the active-task lookup (including next_open_item and completed_items), and the stdout hook-output shape together.
invariants: No relay through claude-hooks and no new daemon — registers as one more independent PostToolUse hook entry alongside claude-hooks' own client.py and concept_store/diff_hook.py

task-framework remains sole owner of the active-task/drift decision even though claude-hooks supplies the raw call count — this module and dispatcher.drift_reflection_nudge are the only place that decides whether a given call fires
drift-hook-posttooluse-entrypoint.name: drift-hook-posttooluse-entrypoint

contracts: loop_debt(store, limit=10) -> {tasks_examined, skipped_introspection, ungraded_risks} — the cheap window mcp_server._loop_debt_hook reads on every tasks__set_active call (task:07f9270c), using a smaller limit than grooming_accuracy's default 25 since set_active fires far more often per session.
grooming_accuracy(store, limit) -> tallies, recurring risks, skipped introspections, self-report disagreements, and signals
Scoped to status='done' only
Everything except `signals` is a raw count or a list of task ids
Exposed as tasks__grooming_accuracy
grooming-accuracy-aggregate.description: Aggregates grooming risk grades across recent finished tasks — the only read that spans tasks rather than descending into one. Closes the feedback edge at the level of the loop itself: without it, 'repeated wrong grades mean grooming asks the wrong questions' is advice nothing can act on, because grades live inside each task and a pattern across tasks was writable but unreadable.
invariants: _task_grading(task) -> (risks, ungraded_count, any_graded) is the single per-task classification both grooming_accuracy and loop_debt call — factored out (task:07f9270c) so the two reads can never disagree about what counts as skipped or ungraded.
Tallies are DERIVED from per-risk `graded` values and never read from an introspection report's self-reported grooming_accuracy count — the same reason progress is derived from the checklist
A disagreement between the self-reported tally and the derived one is reported, never silently resolved
risks.total counts every risk seen, independently of the grade buckets, so an unrecognised grade cannot make a risk vanish from the total
An unrecognised grade is bucketed and reported rather than dropped
Only a FINISHED task with ungraded risks is a skipped introspection; an open one is work in progress
predictive_value excludes ungraded risks from its denominator, so skipping the grading never flatters the score
Ratio signals require MIN_SAMPLE graded risks; the skipped-introspection signal requires no sample, because one is already the loop not running
A risk recurs only across DISTINCT tasks — a repeat within one task is a duplicate, not a pattern

Recurrence groups by a risk's id when it has one (task:f24be6e4) and falls back to normalised text only for id-less (pre-migration) risks; each recurring_risks entry reports keyed_by so a caller can tell which grouping produced it.

Because ids are assigned per-risk rather than shared across tasks, two occurrences of the 'same' risk written independently in different tasks will not recur under id-keying unless one was reworded forward from the other — a known, accepted limitation recorded as an open risk on task:f24be6e4, not yet resolved.
grooming-accuracy-aggregate.name: grooming-accuracy-aggregate

contracts: grooming_accuracy(store) and loop_debt(store) must agree on skipped_introspection count and ungraded risk count for the same tasks (task:07f9270c).
grooming-accuracy-derived-not-self-repor.description: Pins two properties of taskfw.accuracy.grooming_accuracy: risk tallies are always derived from per-risk `graded` fields rather than trusted from an introspection report's self-reported counts, and a finished task with ungraded risks is surfaced as a skipped-introspection signal distinct from a task with zero risks. Both are silent-failure classes a passing implementation could otherwise mask.
invariants: Tallies must be recomputed from grooming.risks[].graded on every call, never read from introspection[].grooming_accuracy.
A finished task with any ungraded risk appears in skipped_introspection; an open task with ungraded risks never does.
grooming-accuracy-derived-not-self-repor.name: grooming-accuracy-derived-not-self-reported

lifecycle-rules-pure-function-testing.description: Protects taskfw.lifecycle's rules being pure functions over plain values (statuses, Task instances) with no store or session dependency -- the test module needs no fixtures at all, which is itself the property: the moment a rule needed a session or host, it would stop being importable by every caller (MCP tools, hooks, migration) uniformly.
invariants: check_transition, check_parent, check_type, check_status, check_link_rel, and check_save take only plain values/Task objects and a Decision return type -- no store, connection, or session argument.
Same-status transitions are always allowed even from a terminal state, and this precedence (same-status beats terminal-lock) is checked ahead of the terminal rule.
check_save evaluates type before parent before transition, so the first failing rule is always the one reported.
parent_of is deliberately excluded from the closed relation set enforced by check_link_rel, since it is redundant with Task.parent.
lifecycle-rules-pure-function-testing.name: lifecycle-rules-pure-function-testing

contracts: Every check returns Decision(allowed, rule, reason); Decision is falsy when denied
check_save(task, previous=None, parent=None) is the single entry point for validating a mutation

check_link_rel(rel) -> Decision gates tasks__link only, denying any rel not in TASK_EDGE_RELATIONS — mirrors check_status(status)'s exact closed-set-against-a-tuple shape. Deliberately NOT called from tasks__unlink: removal must always work for a legacy or out-of-vocabulary rel, or a bad historical row becomes permanently stuck (task:1c9d37d7).
There is no check_active_switch anymore (removed task:f302eb2b) — tasks__set_active/push_active is non-destructive by construction, so nothing needs confirm=True to avoid losing state
lifecycle-single-rule-implementation.description: The single implementation of every task rule, imported by both the MCP tools and the hooks. Pure functions over (inputs, store) with no session, prompt, or host state. Deliberately small: body-template validation became schema validation, the hierarchy matrix collapsed to one sentence with two issue types, and commit traceability left entirely once the pre-commit gate was dropped. check_active_switch was deleted outright in task:f302eb2b once the active-task pointer became a non-destructive LIFO stack (push_active) instead of a single overwritten value — there was nothing left to guard against losing.
invariants: Rules are pure — the tests need no fixtures at all, which is the observable signal that portability holds
Same-status is checked BEFORE the terminal rule, so re-saving a done or abandoned task is never an error; this is what makes tasks__finish idempotent
done and abandoned are terminal; any non-terminal state may be abandoned
The entire hierarchy rule is: an epic has no parent, and a task cannot be its own parent
Denials log at INFO with rule, reason, and ids; allows log at DEBUG
check_link_rel is the FIRST policy check ever added to tasks__link — before task:1c9d37d7 it had zero lifecycle validation, calling store().link() directly after only confirming both task ids exist

tasks__finish/tasks__check_item's auto-finish share one _finish_task() helper (mcp_server.py) that pops the active-task stack only when the finished task_id is on top — a buried finish still marks the task done, it just skips the pop (task:f302eb2b)
lifecycle-single-rule-implementation.name: lifecycle-single-rule-implementation

log-sink-thread-safety-and-fail-open-tes.description: Regression coverage for task:7fff42f4: SQLiteHandler must never let a broken or cross-thread connection break the call that triggered the log write. A single process-wide sqlite3 connection reused across an MCP server's worker threads raises ProgrammingError from a thread that did not create it; SQLiteHandler.emit's bare except previously swallowed that silently for the rest of the process, so the fix (threading.local, one connection per thread) makes the reuse unrepresentable instead of catching it after the fact. Also pins JsonlHandler's truncate-on-construct behavior and that the taskfw logger never attaches a stdout stream handler, since an MCP server speaks JSON-RPC on stdout and a stray log write would corrupt it.
invariants: SQLiteHandler.emit() never raises, even against a broken connection object or from a second thread -- it must keep working via one connection per thread (threading.local), not merely swallow the failure.
No handler on the 'taskfw' logger ever has stream is sys.stdout.
JsonlHandler truncates its target file at construction time, and a log call landing in the module-level get_logger() actually writes to TASKFW_LOG_JSONL during test runs.
tasks__logs(logger=...) matching requires the full 'taskfw.' prefix taskfw.log.get_logger() always applies -- a caller-supplied name missing that prefix matches nothing.
log-sink-thread-safety-and-fail-open-tes.name: log-sink-thread-safety-and-fail-open-tested

logging-one-line-explainability-tested.description: Pins the debuggability contract that a rule denial or a store state change must be explicable from a single log line, including the ids and states involved -- asserted directly rather than assumed, because logging that is not tested rots invisibly (nothing fails when a log line silently loses its rule name or its id).
invariants: A lifecycle DENY logs at INFO with the rule name, a human reason, and the states/ids involved; ALLOW is DEBUG-only and invisible at INFO.

TaskStore logs CREATE with the new id, STATUS with both old and new status, link/unlink with a removed=N count, and a duplicate link as 'already existed' -- all distinguishable by substring in caplog.text.
A plain field update (no status change) logs at DEBUG only, never emitting CREATE or STATUS at INFO.
logging-one-line-explainability-tested.name: logging-one-line-explainability-tested

contracts: record(slug, text, task_id, kind) requires a real task; re-recording a slug updates the text and adds the new source
recall(query, kind, limit, include_superseded, count_hit) excludes superseded memories by default
link(slug, task_id, relation) records confirmed_by / contradicted_by / learned_from
supersede(slug, by) keeps the row; forget(slug) deletes it
Rejected is raised for shape errors only; the store enforces no policy
Exposed as task_memory__record / recall / get / link / supersede / forget, and read (not written) by taskfw/context.py:lessons_for

recall(query=...) matches by ORing the query's whitespace-split terms (not FTS5's default implicit AND) and orders results by bm25(memories_fts) relevance; the empty-query 'list recent' path is the only one still ordered by updated_at
recall()'s default limit is DEFAULT_RECALL_LIMIT (5), defined in taskfw/config.py and env-overridable via TASKFW_DEFAULT_RECALL_LIMIT — not a literal in memory.py

recall(count_hit=False) performs the same search with the counter write suppressed (task:60ebca8e). It exists for exactly one caller, context.lessons_for: bundle assembly is not a deliberate reach for a lesson, so counting it would leave hit_count measuring tasks__context calls with no way to separate the two afterwards. The default stays True, so every deliberate task_memory__recall still counts.

memories_fts indexes 'slug text' and has NO tags column — relevant because context.lessons_for reuses related_candidates' 'title + tags' query string, where tags carry a 3:1 weighting on the tasks side that has no equivalent here
loop-memory-derived-standing.description: Memory scoped to the loop: the lessons introspection produces that nothing else can hold — a constraint discovered the hard way, a technique worth reusing, a recurring pitfall. Graded risks, decisions, and architectural facts already have homes, so this deliberately covers only what is left over, and must not grow into a general knowledge store. As of task:60ebca8e it also has a guaranteed read path: the `lessons` section of tasks__context.
invariants: Standing is DERIVED from the confirm/contradict links on every read and is never stored — a stored confidence would agree with whatever was typed

A `disputed` memory is reported as disputed rather than resolved: the store cannot know which side is right, and returning it as settled would be an omission indistinguishable from an absence. This now matters more than it did: a disputed lesson arrives unasked-for inside every full tasks__context bundle, so the marking is what stops it reading as settled fact.
Every memory cites the task it was learned from — an uncited lesson is an opinion and cannot be checked against the work that produced it
Superseding keeps the row and names the replacement; forgetting is reserved for a lesson that was WRONG rather than outdated
Superseded memories leave recall by default, because stale knowledge that keeps surfacing reads as current — and therefore never appear in a context bundle's lessons either, for free
Links are idempotent, so re-running introspection cannot inflate a memory's standing

Lives in the task database as one file rather than a second store; the memory-to-task citation is validated at the tool layer, NOT by a foreign key, so the single file is about having one source to check rather than about referential integrity. context.lessons_for depends on this: it opens a MemoryStore straight from store.conn when no instance is passed.

Nothing is injected, but a memory now reaches an agent two ways: task_memory__recall, and the `lessons` section of a full tasks__context bundle (task:60ebca8e). Both are pulls — the agent called the tool — so the pull-not-push bargain is intact; what changed is that reading lessons back no longer depends on the agent independently remembering the recall tool exists. This supersedes the earlier invariant 'a memory reaches an agent only via task_memory__recall'.
A malformed FTS5 query falls back to an unranked LIKE match rather than being treated as proof no memories exist

hit_count/last_hit are purely observational usage signals, not staleness inputs — nothing currently reads them to drive supersede/forget automation (see task:582dba10, open). They count DELIBERATE recalls only: context bundle assembly passes count_hit=False precisely so the signal task:582dba10 would consume stays uncontaminated by automatic reads.
loop-memory-derived-standing.name: loop-memory-derived-standing

contracts: Every tool returns a dict; a refusal is {'error': reason, 'rule': which_rule}
mcp-portable-interface.description: The portable interface: MCP is the portability layer, so any MCP host reaches the whole framework through these tools with no neutral abstraction on top. Tools are in-process -- they import the library directly, with no daemon and no transport. Every mutating tool validates through lifecycle before calling store. Three narrower concepts hold this module's detail: [[mcp-tool-registration-and-hooks]] (the _tool decorator and its hook wiring), [[active-task-pointer-lifecycle]] (the single in-memory active-task pointer), and [[task-tool-response-shapes]] (per-tool response contracts).
invariants: No tool enforces a rule itself -- all validation goes through lifecycle.check_*, so a tool cannot enforce a different set than a hook
The store is opened lazily, so importing the module never touches disk
Active-task scope comes from TASKFW_SCOPE or cwd, never from a stored global
mcp-portable-interface.name: mcp-portable-interface

contracts: _tool(hook=None) is the single decorator every tool carries instead of @mcp.tool(): it wraps fn in dispatcher.tool_called(fn.__name__, post=hook) and registers the WRAPPED function with mcp.tool() itself, so the module-level name bound is the logged version too. Plain tools use @_tool(); tools needing one or more nudges pass @_tool(hook=some_hook) or @_tool(hook=dispatcher.combine(hook_a, hook_b)).

The 5 hook functions (_finish_reminder_hook, _ungroomed_progress_hook, _finish_hook, _stale_memory_hook, _introspection_hook) are all Callable[[dict], None], defined once near _tool and referenced by name at each tool's own decorator line -- never centrally dispatched by tool name. Hooks that need the post-mutation task re-fetch it via store().get(result['id']) rather than closing over a local variable computed mid-function, since the mutation is already persisted (store().save() already ran) by the time any hook fires -- this is what let hook-bearing and plain tools converge on one decorator instead of two different wiring mechanisms (task:58782207).
mcp-tool-registration-and-hooks.description: Pulled out of [[mcp-portable-interface]]. Every one of the ~35 registered tools is wrapped in dispatcher.tool_called for unconditional logging via a single mechanism, mcp_server._tool -- the one route every tool goes through for registration + logging + an optional post-success hook. A tool skips registration entirely if it skips _tool; there is no 'registered but unlogged' state.
invariants: No tool is missing the _tool wrapper and none is double-wrapped -- pinned by tests/test_mcp_tools.py::TestToolCallLogging, which enumerates the live m.mcp.list_tools() registry rather than a hand-maintained list, so a new tool that forgets the decorator fails this test rather than silently going unlogged

There is no drift-reflection hook left in this module (task:8be768df removed _drift_reflection_hook entirely) -- drift-reflection awareness now lives solely in taskfw/drift_hook.py, a standalone PostToolUse hook Claude Code invokes directly on every tool call in the session, independent of any MCP tool call.

_introspection_hook checks dispatcher.is_introspected(task) rather than the raw task.introspection truthy test it used before (task:f6be04bf's audit) -- consolidating on task-phase-derivation's single-source predicate rather than re-testing the field, matching finish_nudge/ungroomed_progress_nudge's own consolidation in nudges.py.
mcp-tool-registration-and-hooks.name: mcp-tool-registration-and-hooks

contracts: Tools call taskfw.lifecycle for every rule check rather than re-implementing it (task-framework's one-rule-one-place constraint).
mcp-tools-enforce-nothing-themselves.description: Protects the property that MCP tools carry no rule logic of their own -- every check a tool result reflects (transition validity, parent rules, relation closed-set) is delegated to taskfw.lifecycle, so a tool cannot silently enforce a different rule set than a hook or the migration path does. Tools are exercised by calling the decorated functions directly (MCPServer's decorator returns them unchanged), which reaches the same code path a real host transport does without standing up JSON-RPC.
invariants: Every rule-shaped refusal returned by a tasks__ tool traces back to a taskfw.lifecycle Decision, not to logic duplicated in mcp_server.py.
Calling a registered tool function directly (bypassing any transport) exercises the identical code path a real MCP host would invoke through the decorator.

drift_reflection_nudge never appears as a key on any mcp_server tool result -- its trigger lives solely in taskfw/drift_hook.py's separate PostToolUse hook, so the two paths cannot silently coexist and disagree.
mcp-tools-enforce-nothing-themselves.name: mcp-tools-enforce-nothing-themselves

memory-standing-and-recall-tests-pinned.description: Protects two properties of taskfw.memory: standing (unverified/confirmed/contradicted/disputed) is always derived from confirmed_by/contradicted_by links at read time, never stored or self-asserted, matching the same derive-don't-trust discipline taskfw.accuracy enforces elsewhere. A disputed memory (both a confirming and a contradicting link) is reported as disputed rather than silently resolved one way, since the store has no basis to pick a side.
invariants: MemoryStore.get()/recall() compute standing solely from memory_links rows at call time; nothing in the memories table stores a standing value.
A memory with both confirmed_by and contradicted_by links reports standing='disputed', never silently collapsing to one side.
Linking the same (slug, task, relation) twice is a no-op (returns False the second time) and does not duplicate the id in confirmed_by/contradicted_by.
record() rejects non-kebab-case slugs, unknown kinds, and text shorter than MIN_TEXT (a label masquerading as a lesson) via Rejected.
memory-standing-and-recall-tests-pinned.name: memory-standing-and-recall-tests-pinned

memory-supersede-hides-by-default-tested.description: Pins that a superseded memory leaves recall() by default but the row itself survives and names its replacement -- stale knowledge that keeps surfacing reads as current and is worse than none, so supersede() must actually hide it from the default recall path while still being reachable via include_superseded=True, and forget() must cascade to delete its links so no standing points at a memory that no longer exists.
invariants: memories.recall() excludes superseded memories unless include_superseded=True is passed explicitly.
supersede(old, new) leaves the old row in place with superseded_by=new and standing='superseded'; it never deletes the row.
A memory cannot supersede itself, and superseding by an unknown slug is rejected.
forget(slug) deletes memory_links rows referencing that slug along with the memory row -- no orphaned link survives the memory it points at.
memory-supersede-hides-by-default-tested.name: memory-supersede-hides-by-default-tested

methodology-docs-tool-references-verifie.description: Guards against the docs describing an API that no longer exists -- the most likely and most silent failure mode for prose documentation. Every tasks__/task_memory__ token found in docs/methodology/*.md is checked against the tool names actually registered on taskfw.mcp_server, and the docs are further checked for host-prefixed tool names or a session_id concept, both signs the prose still describes the prior system this framework replaced.
invariants: Every tasks__ or task_memory__ token appearing in any methodology doc must name a tool actually present on taskfw.mcp_server (registered_tools() reads dir(m), never a restated list).
No methodology doc contains 'mcp__claude-hooks__' (a host-prefixed tool name) or 'session_id' (a concept this framework has no notion of).
Every markdown-to-markdown link within docs/methodology resolves to a file that exists, and README.md indexes every other document in the directory.
The docs explicitly state both 'pull' and 'inject' somewhere in README.md, since a reader coming from an injection-based system needs the pull-not-push distinction stated, not implied.
methodology-docs-tool-references-verifie.name: methodology-docs-tool-references-verified-by-test

migrate-hooks-idempotency-regression-pin.description: Every assertion in this file corresponds to a claim the claude-hooks-to-taskfw migration makes about itself in prose, run rather than trusted. The idempotency test exists because that prose was wrong on the first live run: tasks upsert by id and edges/commits have natural keys, but task_events has an autoincrement id with nothing to collide against, so a second run silently duplicated 4072 event rows in a real database -- nothing caught it except actually running the migration twice and counting rows.
invariants: Running taskfw.migrate_hooks.migrate() two or three times against the same source produces identical table row counts each time (idempotency), including for task_events which has no natural key.
migrated + empty + orphaned counts must sum to the total source rows for events, edges, and commits -- a dropped row nothing reports is indistinguishable from one that never existed.
A parent cycle in the source is reported via report.unplaceable rather than silently reparented or dropped, and produces zero migrated tasks.
dry_run=True computes and reports counts without writing any row to the destination tables.
migrate-hooks-idempotency-regression-pin.name: migrate-hooks-idempotency-regression-pinned

migrate-hooks-type-collapse-preserves-re.description: Pins how the migration collapses claude-hooks' five issue types (epic/story/bug/subtask/feedback) and a 'review' status down into taskfw's two-type, four-status model without losing information: the dropped label is preserved as a data tag rather than discarded outright, and a structurally impossible shape (an epic with a parent) is demoted to a task while its real parent relationship is kept, never orphaned.
invariants: story/bug/subtask/feedback all become type='task' in taskfw, with the original type name preserved inside the task's data as a tag (e.g. 'was-story').

An epic that had a parent in the source is demoted to type='task' with its parent preserved and 'was-epic' recorded in data -- the relationship is never dropped to satisfy the epic-cannot-have-parent rule.
status='review' becomes 'open' with 'was-review' recorded in data.
Body checklist markup ('- [x]'/'- [ ]') is parsed into typed ResolutionItem entries and the raw body is also preserved verbatim in notes.
migrate-hooks-type-collapse-preserves-re.name: migrate-hooks-type-collapse-preserves-relationships

migration-writes-through-the-store.description: One-time import of claude-hooks' task store (~/.claude/proj_tasks.db) into taskfw. Every task is written through TaskStore.save() rather than by raw INSERT, because tasks.data holds the typed object while the scalar columns are projected from it, and save() is the sole writer of both. A bulk INSERT here would be a second writer whose rows disagree with themselves the moment either side changes. Side tables (events, edges, commits) are inserted directly since they carry no projected duplication. The type collapse is lossy by decision, not by accident: five claude-hooks issue types become taskfw's two, with the original preserved as a tag, because the extra four enforced no rule and were therefore already labels.
invariants: Tasks are written only through TaskStore.save(), never by direct INSERT into tasks
Re-running changes nothing: save() upserts by id and side tables use INSERT OR IGNORE against their natural keys
Parents are saved before children; a row whose parent is missing or cyclic is reported as unplaceable, never silently reparented
Every source row is accounted for in the Report — migrated, empty, or orphaned — so a dropped row is never indistinguishable from one that never existed
No status outside STATUSES is ever written; an unrecognised one becomes open and is tagged with what it was
migration-writes-through-the-store.name: migration-writes-through-the-store

model-provenance-stamp-enforced-by-test.description: Enforces the @ModelProvenance stamps every models/*.sysml package carries: each declares modelledPaths (the code it describes) and derivedFromCommit (the commit it was last read against), and this test checks both against git so a failure means the model has not been re-read since the modelled code moved -- not that the model is wrong. Bumping derivedFromCommit without re-reading the package would convert a useful drift signal into a lie, which the test's own docstring calls out as worse than having no stamp.
invariants: Every models/*.sysml file has an @ModelProvenance stamp with a derivedFromCommit of at least 7 hex characters and a non-empty modelledPaths list.

Every path in modelledPaths must exist in the working tree -- a cited path that was deleted is drift the commit-comparison check alone cannot catch, since git log over a deleted path still resolves and may match the stamp.

derivedFromCommit must equal (or be an ancestor consistent with) the last commit that touched any of modelledPaths, per `git log -1 -- <paths>`; a mismatch means the model is stale relative to the code, not necessarily wrong.
Checks skip gracefully (not fail) when not in a git checkout, when git log returns nothing for the paths, or when the stamped commit isn't present in a shallow clone's history.
model-provenance-stamp-enforced-by-test.name: model-provenance-stamp-enforced-by-test

contracts: tool_called(name, pre=None, post=None): context manager wrapping one MCP tool call. `pre` runs on entry. `post` runs once, after the block exits with no exception and call.result is a dict not containing an 'error' key (a refusal). A non-dict result (e.g. tasks__list's bare list) is treated as success for logging but never invokes `post`, since apply_nudge needs a dict to write into.
Exactly one log line per exit: 'tool=<name> OK' / 'tool=<name> REFUSE rule=<rule>' / 'tool=<name> ERROR <type>: <msg>' at INFO level, no arguments or payloads logged.

combine(*hooks) -> Callable[[dict], None]: runs each hook in order against the same result dict, letting a tool that needs several nudges (e.g. tasks__update) compose them at its own call site rather than tool_called/_tool needing a multi-hook parameter.

apply_nudge(result, key, nudge) sets result[key] = nudge only if nudge is truthy, and logs the firing there — so any nudge added later is observable in the logs table for free, without remembering a log line at each new call site.
nudge-dispatch-chassis.description: Shared machinery every advisory nudge runs through: unconditional per-call tool logging (tool_called), hook composition (combine), and the one shared result-mutation helper (apply_nudge). Distinct from the nudge functions' own firing policies — see [[advisory-nudge-policies]] — and from [[task-phase-derivation]]'s pure state helpers. Extracted from the flat taskfw/dispatcher.py into taskfw/dispatcher/chassis.py; taskfw/dispatcher/__init__.py re-exports every name so `from taskfw import dispatcher` and `from taskfw.dispatcher import tool_called` are unaffected by the split.
invariants: Never blocks or changes a write — advisory only, for both the chassis and everything it dispatches to.

No name-keyed dispatch table (no GATES-style registry) — explicitly reconsidered and rejected during task:58782207's design pass: a registry would let a rename silently desync a string key from the tool it names and accretes per-tool conditions into the table itself. Every hook stays local and explicit at its own tool's decorator line in mcp_server.py, composed via combine() when more than one applies.

Every one of mcp_server.py's registered tools produces exactly one tool_called log line per call — verified by tests/test_mcp_tools.py::TestToolCallLogging::test_every_registered_tool_logs_exactly_once_when_called, which enumerates the live m.mcp.list_tools() registry rather than a hand-maintained list.

Call sites build `post` with a lambda, not functools.partial: apply_nudge takes `result` first, but partial appends new positional args after the pre-bound ones, so partial(apply_nudge, key, nudge) called as p(result) would call apply_nudge(key, nudge, result) — wrong order.

chassis.py imports nothing from nudges.py or phase.py — it is pure mechanism operating only on a Callable[[dict], None] hook and a result dict, never on task state itself; that is what keeps it the one module none of the others need to change when a nudge's condition changes.
nudge-dispatch-chassis.name: nudge-dispatch-chassis

contracts: build_context(store, task_id, verbosity, memory=None) -> bundle, or {'error': ...} for an unknown task. `memory` is an optional MemoryStore; when omitted, build_context opens one from store.conn, since memories share the task database. mcp_server.tasks__context passes the shared singleton on purpose — MemoryStore.__init__ runs CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and commits, so constructing one per call would put a write on a pure read path. NOTE the parameter is optional rather than required for call-site compatibility (task:60ebca8e decision), so the write-on-read failure mode is mitigated at the one production call site, not deleted; a second production caller should make it required.
Sections in fixed order: task, decisions, grooming, graph, commits, related, lessons
verbosity='summary' returns identity, status, progress, and open items only — it carries no lessons section, and returns before any MemoryStore is opened

graph.edges is capped at MAX_EDGES (5) per direction (outgoing/incoming independently), sliced in _graph(); when either direction is capped, the drop counts are reported in a bundle-level `edges_truncated` dict, e.g. {'outgoing': 3, 'incoming': 2}

related_candidates(store, task) (public, renamed from _related in task:78853657) passes task.title straight through as a plain string to store.search() -- search() itself builds the OR-of-terms FTS5 query AND ranks by _combination_score (tag overlap weighted 3x over body overlap), not bm25 `rank` as of task:f24a88e3. As of task:1f1e48e2 it over-fetches MAX_RELATED*4+1 hits and filters them through _passes_floor before slicing to MAX_RELATED, so ranking alone no longer determines what surfaces.

lessons_for(store, task, memory=None) (public, task:60ebca8e) queries MemoryStore.recall with the same 'title + tags' string related_candidates uses, over-fetching MAX_LESSONS*4 rows (task:1f1e48e2) and filtering through the same _passes_floor before slicing to MAX_LESSONS. Rows that pass are returned unmodified so each lesson carries the `standing` derived in the memory store. It calls recall(count_hit=False): assembling a bundle must not bump hit_count/last_hit, which exist to measure DELIBERATE recall.

_passes_floor(query_terms, candidate_text) -> bool (task:1f1e48e2) is the ONE relevance-floor predicate shared by both related_candidates and lessons_for, deliberately not reimplemented per call site or per scorer. It requires at least one word of _MIN_TERM_LEN (4) or more letters shared between query and candidate text, via _term_set — a plain lowercase-word-set overlap check, chosen over a score threshold or a cutoff relative to the top hit because it is the one form that works unchanged across store.search()'s _combination_score and memories_fts's bm25, two scores that are neither comparable to each other nor stable as the corpus grows. Purely-numeric tokens (e.g. "2026" from a tag like introspection-2026-08-23) are excluded from _term_set so two same-day items don't pass the floor on a meaningless date collision. If the query itself has no word meeting the length floor, _passes_floor returns True (permissive) rather than rejecting everything — there is no vocabulary to test candidates against in that case.
pull-context-bundle.description: build_context assembles the whole working bundle for a task in one call — the sole replacement for per-turn prompt injection. Fixed section order, a documented trim order dropping whole sections least-useful-first, and a truncated list so an omitted section is distinguishable from an empty one. Independently, several sections also carry a fixed per-section cap (MAX_DECISIONS, MAX_COMMITS, MAX_RELATED, MAX_LESSONS, MAX_EDGES) applied by slicing before CHAR_BUDGET enforcement ever runs — a separate, silent mechanism from the whole-section drop that TRIM_ORDER implements, except for edges: edges' cap is the one case that IS surfaced, via `edges_truncated`. As of task:60ebca8e the bundle has a seventh section, `lessons`, which is the guaranteed read path for loop memory. As of task:1f1e48e2, related and lessons both filter through a shared relevance floor before their caps are applied.
invariants: The task section is NEVER trimmed — a bundle without its task is useless rather than merely large

CHAR_BUDGET-driven trimming (_enforce_budget) drops whole sections, never parts of one, for every section EXCEPT grooming: a half-listed set of commits/related/lessons/graph/decisions reads as complete and is more misleading than an absent section that says so. Anything dropped whole is named in `truncated`.

grooming is the one section trimmed field-by-field instead of whole (task:1c31a060, fixing a measured cost on task:60ebca8e: grooming was 8371 chars against task=4087/decisions=1890, so whole-section dropping evicted it entirely and landed the bundle at 6155 chars with 5845 unspent — the more thoroughly a task was groomed, the more certainly its grooming vanished from the main entry point, breaking introspection's ability to grade its own predictions). _trim_grooming now drops grooming's own fields least-useful-first per GROOMING_TRIM_ORDER (suggested_improvements, prior_art, hidden_assumptions, risks, open_questions, clarifications — clarifications last, being verified facts, the highest-value content grooming produces) until the bundle fits or grooming has nothing left. Fields actually dropped are named in `grooming_truncated`, a field distinct from `truncated` for the same reason `edges_truncated` is: a caller reading only the response can tell partial grooming from complete grooming, and knows not to round-trip a partial dict through tasks__update's wholesale-replace. Only if grooming trims down to {} does it fall through to a normal whole-section drop and get named in `truncated` like every other section.

Separately, MAX_DECISIONS/MAX_COMMITS/MAX_RELATED/MAX_LESSONS apply a fixed pre-slice cap regardless of CHAR_BUDGET, and do so SILENTLY — none of them appear in `truncated` when the fixed cap (not the budget) is what cut the list. This is a known asymmetry, not yet resolved for the other four.

MAX_EDGES is the one fixed cap on a non-grooming section that reports its own truncation, via `edges_truncated` — a field distinct from `truncated` on purpose: `truncated` means CHAR_BUDGET dropped a whole section, `edges_truncated` means the section is present but its edges list was capped
If CHAR_BUDGET forces `graph` to drop entirely, `edges_truncated` is cleared too, so a truncation count can never outlive the section it describes

related and lessons are the TWO approximate sections and the first two trimmed, in that order (TRIM_ORDER = related, lessons, commits, graph, grooming, decisions). Every other section is an exact lookup — grooming included, despite now being trimmed like an approximate one; its position in TRIM_ORDER and its exactness are unrelated to whether it can be partially rendered.

As of task:1f1e48e2, related and lessons both exclude, not merely rank low, a candidate with no meaningful term overlap — fixing the case where ranking-without-exclusion always filled both sections to their cap with the best-available match, however weak (observed live, task:60ebca8e: a task about loop memory drew 'Remove LLM from certificate renewal flow' as related and three off-topic memories as lessons). The 'title + tags' QUERY SHAPE itself is unchanged and still has the failure mode task:60ebca8e's introspection found: it describes what a task IS about, not what it needs to KNOW, so it can still admit a weak match that happens to share a long word for the wrong reason, and can still miss a strong match whose vocabulary the title/tags don't contain. The floor fixes the exclusion half of that gap, not the query-shape half — that remains open, deliberately deferred rather than silently dropped (task:1f1e48e2 decision).

lessons is always a list, never a dict — so that _enforce_budget's isinstance branch resets it to [] and an omitted lessons section stays distinguishable from a task that simply has no matching memories. grooming is the one section that is a dict, which is exactly why it needed its own trim path (_trim_grooming) rather than reusing the list-based isinstance branch.

Building a bundle has NO write side effect on loop memory: hit_count and last_hit are untouched by tasks__context, so they keep measuring deliberate task_memory__recall only (pinned by tests/test_context.py::TestLessons::test_assembling_a_bundle_does_not_bump_hit_count)
pull-context-bundle.name: pull-context-bundle

contracts: migrate(conn) -> {'created': [...], 'added': ['table.column'], 'orphaned': ['table.column']}
Table.create_sql() generates DDL from the same columns migration diffs against
schema-single-source-additive-migration.description: TABLES is one declarative structure of Table/Column dataclasses that generates DDL, drives migration, and is read directly by tests. migrate() creates missing tables and adds missing columns, reporting created/added/orphaned. Additive-only is enforced by construction rather than policy: no code path emits DROP or a rewriting ALTER.
invariants: Only CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN are ever emitted
A column present in the DB but absent from TABLES is reported as orphaned and never dropped
There is exactly one DDL definition — tests read TABLES rather than restating it, so no schema-parity check is needed
ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN cannot take a non-constant DEFAULT, so _addable_decl strips it; a migrated column is therefore not byte-identical to the same column created fresh
schema-single-source-additive-migration.name: schema-single-source-additive-migration

skills-tool-reference-and-host-neutralit.description: Guards the one mechanical failure that has already happened once: the .claude/skills wrappers were carried over verbatim from a prior system and referenced roughly a dozen tools that do not exist here, a session_id concept the framework lacks, and a host-prefixed mcp__ namespace -- nothing caught it until a person read the files. This test makes that class of drift fail the suite instead, the same bargain test_concepts.py makes for concept coverage. It does not check whether a skill's prose still agrees with its methodology doc or with other skills -- that judgment call belongs to /task-skills-audit.
invariants: Every tasks__/task_memory__/concept__ token referenced in a skill.md must name a tool actually registered on taskfw.mcp_server.
No skill other than task-skills-audit (which must exist exactly once, as the sole enumerator of these prohibitions) may contain an mcp__ host-prefixed tool name or the string 'session_id'.

Every skill's frontmatter carries name/description/user-invocable/updated/doc, its name matches its directory, its doc: field points at a methodology file that exists, and its frontmatter never names an external checkout (e.g. 'claude-hooks').

Every methodology stage document (0*.md) is referenced by at least one skill's doc: field, and tasks__grooming_accuracy -- the one cross-task tool with no natural discovery path -- is mentioned by at least one skill.
skills-tool-reference-and-host-neutralit.name: skills-tool-reference-and-host-neutrality-tested

contracts: get_logger(name) -> logger under the 'taskfw' root, configured on first call
Level comes from TASKFW_LOG_LEVEL, default INFO
SQLiteHandler and JsonlHandler both swallow every write exception — a broken log write must never break the tool call that triggered it

SQLiteHandler caches one sqlite3 connection per thread (threading.local()), not one per process — a single process-wide connection eventually gets used from a thread that didn't create it (an MCP server dispatches sync tool calls across a worker thread pool), and sqlite3 raises ProgrammingError on that, which the bare except silently swallows for the rest of the process's life (task:7fff42f4)
stderr-only-logging.description: Stderr is always one of the sinks, configured once. An MCP server speaks JSON-RPC over stdout, so a stray write there corrupts the protocol — that is a correctness constraint for the whole project, not a formatting preference, and it bans stdout specifically, not persistence generally. A second sink also exists: SQLiteHandler persists into the `logs` table (the operational-trace half of observability, alongside task_events' durable record of decisions and outcomes) in normal operation, or JsonlHandler when TASKFW_LOG_JSONL is set (test runs only, via tests/conftest.py) — a test run must never add a row to `logs`, isolated database or not, so it writes one JSON-per-line file instead, truncated fresh per run.
invariants: No handler under the taskfw logger may write to stdout — pinned by tests/test_logging.py
The root taskfw logger does not propagate, so host logging config cannot redirect it to stdout
Denials log at INFO and allows at DEBUG, so a full trace is one env var away and costs nothing normally
SQLiteHandler always targets config.db_path(), never whatever TaskStore is currently active — log.py's handlers are process-wide singletons with no store to draw a per-call path from

A SQLiteHandler instance never uses the same sqlite3 connection object across two threads — each thread that calls emit() gets its own connection via threading.local(), so cross-thread reuse (the cause of a total, silent, permanent log-sink death) is unrepresentable rather than merely caught
stderr-only-logging.name: stderr-only-logging

contracts: A port def enumerating an RPC/tool surface (e.g. mcp_interface.sysml's TasksPort/ConceptPort/TaskMemoryPort) is checked by enumerating the LIVE registry at test time (e.g. asyncio.run(m.mcp.list_tools())) rather than importing a static name list, since the registry itself is the source of truth for what is currently registered, not a constant a human could also hand-copy.
sysml-doc-only-model-enforcement.description: SysML v2 structural models in this repo (state defs, calc defs, interface defs/port defs) are transcribed by hand from Python source rather than parsed/bound to it. They are kept honest not by execution but by a paired pytest class that imports the real Python source of truth and string-matches its identifiers/literals against the .sysml file text.
invariants: A calc def or state def with no matching TestXMatchesCode test is an unenforced restatement of the same claim the prose already made — not acceptable per this task's motivation.
Test risk text and grading must stay byte-identical to grooming's `risks` entries for tasks__grooming_accuracy recurrence tracking to work.
sysml-doc-only-model-enforcement.name: sysml-doc-only-model-enforcement

contracts: task_phase(task) -> {groomed, implemented, introspected} (all bool), fully derived every call, never stored — exposed via mcp_server.tasks__phase.

phase_label(phase: dict[str,bool]) -> str collapses task_phase's three independent booleans into a single word — 'grooming' | 'implementation' | 'introspection' | 'done' — by returning the first stage not yet reached in that order.

is_implemented(task) -> bool is the pure predicate (task.progress total>0 and done==total), status-independent — extracted so finish_reminder_nudge and task_phase share one place computing '100% done' instead of two copies that could drift.
next_open_item(task) -> str | None returns the text of the first unchecked resolution item, recomputed from task.resolution on every call.
completed_items(task) -> list[str] returns every checked resolution item's text in checklist order, same non-stored-derivation pattern as next_open_item and is_implemented.

is_groomed(task) -> bool and is_introspected(task) -> bool (task:5a5fde0d) are single-source predicates for task_phase's 'groomed'/'introspected' keys, matching is_implemented's existing precedent — task_phase composes all three rather than re-testing task.grooming/task.introspection inline.
task-phase-derivation.description: Pure, fully-derived task-state helpers shared by [[advisory-nudge-policies]] and mcp_server.py's tasks__phase tool, so neither can disagree about where a task stands in the grooming -> implementation -> introspection loop. Extracted from the flat taskfw/dispatcher.py into taskfw/dispatcher/phase.py; re-exported unchanged from taskfw/dispatcher/__init__.py.
invariants: task_phase's 'groomed' has no separate groomed_at flag — a task is groomed exactly when task.grooming is non-empty, matching task-grooming/skill.md's own definition, so this and ungroomed_progress_nudge can never disagree about what counts as groomed.

is_implemented deliberately excludes finish_reminder_nudge's own status=='open' gate: that gate is about whether to nudge someone to call tasks__finish (pointless once the task is already done), not about whether the work itself is complete — a done task with a full checklist is still implemented.

phase_label makes an ordering call the three booleans themselves don't (a task can be re-groomed after being implemented, introspected without every checklist item done, etc.) — only a caller wanting a single display label (drift_reflection_nudge) needs this; tasks__phase keeps returning the raw booleans so it never disagrees with task_phase itself.

phase_label never throws on a real Task's task_phase() output: grooming/introspection are dataclass fields with default_factory (never None) and progress is a derived property, so the dict it reads is always well-formed (task:afd462e3).

A stored 'current item' pointer could disagree with the checklist the moment an item gets checked off elsewhere; a value recomputed from task.resolution itself cannot, which is why next_open_item and completed_items are never cached.
phase.py has zero imports from chassis.py or nudges.py — it operates only on a Task's own fields, which is what makes it safe for nudges.py to import from without any risk of a cycle.

nudges.py's finish_nudge and ungroomed_progress_nudge call is_introspected(task)/is_groomed(task) rather than testing task.introspection/task.grooming directly (task:5a5fde0d) — every phase-boolean check is coupled to these single predicates, so a future redefinition of what 'groomed' or 'introspected' means changes one function in phase.py instead of requiring every call site to be found and updated independently.
task-phase-derivation.name: task-phase-derivation

task-serialization-contracts-pinned.description: Pins taskfw.task.Task's own serialization and derived-field rules directly, rather than only by proxy through TaskStore's save/load and search tests (which check outcomes like 'a search matched' rather than Task's documented rules themselves). Covers search_text's flattening rules, to_json/from_json round-tripping, from_dict's tolerance of unknown and missing keys, and progress as a purely derived field -- pure Task construction needing no store, the same design point test_lifecycle.py protects for lifecycle rules.
invariants: search_text() concatenates title, motivation, notes, tags, files, and every resolution item's text (done or not) -- falsy fields are omitted entirely rather than appearing as blank segments.
Task.from_dict silently drops unknown keys (forward compatibility with a newer schema) and defaults every missing key (status='open', type='task', resolution=[]) rather than raising.
from_dict converts raw resolution dicts to ResolutionItem instances but passes through already-constructed ResolutionItem objects unchanged.
to_json()/from_json() round-trips every field losslessly, and from_json(None) or from_json('{}') both produce the same default Task as a bare constructor call.
Task.progress is always (done_count, total_count) computed live from resolution -- never a stored field that could drift from it.
task-serialization-contracts-pinned.name: task-serialization-contracts-pinned

contracts: tasks__context with no argument falls back to the active task for the workspace
tasks__finish is idempotent on an already-done task and refuses an abandoned one
tasks__add_introspection appends where tasks__update(grooming=...) replaces
tasks__format_commit_message(task_id, subject, body) validates the task exists and returns the canonical message shape
tasks__logs(logger, level, limit) reads config.db_path() directly via log_conn(), never store().conn

tasks__logs(logger, level, limit) filters by EXACT match only (SQL 'logger=?'/'level=?'), no LIKE/prefix/wildcard support -- auditing a family of related logger names (e.g. every 'taskfw.skill.<name>/<step>' row for one skill) requires either querying each exact name individually or pulling unfiltered rows and filtering client-side by string prefix (verified task:a0bb2c26).
tasks__log_skill_invocation(skill, task_id='') is a thin wrapper around get_logger()
tasks__phase(task_id) returns {id, groomed, implemented, introspected} or {'error': ...} for an unknown task

tasks__create(...) returns {ok, id, type, status} plus an OPTIONAL related_candidates key (list of task summaries, context.related_candidates() against the new task's title) -- present only when at least one candidate is found, omitted entirely otherwise. Advisory only; never creates a tasks__link edge itself (task:78853657).
task-tool-response-shapes.description: Pulled out of [[mcp-portable-interface]]. Per-tool response-shape and semantics contracts for individual tasks__* tools not covered by registration/hooks or active-task mechanics -- context fallback, finish idempotency, introspection append-vs-replace, commit-message formatting, and tasks__logs' exact-match-only log query.
invariants: related_candidates in tasks__create's response is computed inline in the tool body, NOT via the dispatcher hook/nudge mechanism -- every existing nudge is str | None, a candidate list is list[dict], a structurally different shape (task:78853657)
task-tool-response-shapes.name: task-tool-response-shapes

contracts: schema.TASKS declares the 5 scalar columns (id, type, status, parent, title) plus data/created_at/updated_at — adding a 6th scalar means updating BOTH schema.TASKS and the explicit column list in TaskStore.save()'s INSERT/ON CONFLICT statement, which is not derived from TABLES
Task (models.py) is the superset: every schema scalar name (type, status, parent, title, id) must exist as a same-named Task field, or save() breaks on task.<attr> access
TaskStore.save(task) is the ONLY place that writes tasks.type/status/parent/title — no other method in store.py, lifecycle.py, or mcp_server.py issues an UPDATE/INSERT against those columns

TaskStore.list(status=, type=, parent=) and TaskStore.children() filter on the scalar columns only — a field promoted into `data` but not mirrored as a scalar is invisible to these filters and to idx_tasks_status/idx_tasks_parent

TaskStore.get(task_id) and .search() read ONLY the `data` column and reconstruct via Task.from_json — they never read the scalars, so a scalar/data mismatch is invisible to these two paths specifically
tasks-table-projection-contract.description: The tasks table has two kinds of columns that must stay in lockstep: five indexable scalars (id, type, status, parent, title) that mirror fields on Task, and one `data` column holding the full Task as JSON, which is authoritative for every field not promoted to a scalar. There is exactly one writer of both — TaskStore.save() — which is what prevents the projection from drifting. Anything that reads a scalar (tasks__list's status/type/parent filters, the idx_tasks_status/idx_tasks_parent indexes) is reading a value that also exists inside `data`; anything that reads `data` (Task.from_json, every other field) never touches the scalars at all.
invariants: A scalar column name in schema.TASKS that has no matching Task field is a silent breakage point: save() would raise AttributeError on task.<name>, but nothing enforces the two lists match except manual read-through — there is no test pinning column-name/field-name parity the way test_foundation.py pins additive-only migration
Renaming a Task field without renaming the corresponding schema.TASKS column (or vice versa) is exactly the kind of change concept__search on the old/new name should catch before it ships
New Task fields do NOT need a matching scalar column by default — only fields that need to be filtered/indexed independent of JSON parsing get promoted (see schema.py's own comment on TASKS.data)
