schema.migrate()'s additive-only guarantee (see schema-single-source-additive-migration) means a scalar column can be added but never renamed in place — a Task field rename therefore always means a NEW scalar column plus an orphaned old one, not an in-place rename
tasks-table-projection-contract.name: tasks-table-projection-contract

contracts: save(task) upserts and returns the task; get(id) -> Task | None
link() and add_commit() return True when a row was created, False when it already existed
unlink(from_id, to_id, rel=None) -> rows removed; omitting rel removes every edge between the pair
search(query, limit) falls back to LIKE when FTS5 is unavailable or the query is malformed

search(query)'s `query` is a PLAIN string, not pre-formatted FTS5 syntax -- search() builds its own OR-of-terms MATCH expression internally (each term quoted, so punctuation is read as literal text). Callers (tasks__search, context.related_candidates()) never construct FTS syntax themselves.

search() ranks results by _combination_score(task, terms), NOT FTS5's own bm25 `rank` -- tag-word overlap is weighted 3x over body-word overlap (_TAG_WEIGHT/_BODY_WEIGHT), mirroring claude-hooks' LoadMemoriesNode combination scorer (task:c3b53021). FTS5 MATCH still does candidate recall (over-fetched at limit*4); only the final ordering is Python-side (task:f24a88e3).

set_active(task_id, scope)/get_active(scope)/clear_active(scope) replaced push_active/pop_active/active_stack (task:f5ace343) -- a plain in-memory dict (scope -> task_id) on TaskStore, gone the moment the process ends. set_active just overwrites scope's entry; no push/no-op-on-already-top special case. clear_active pops the scope key and logs only if something was actually cleared.
taskstore-data-access-only.description: Persistence for tasks, events, edges, commits, and the active-task pointer. Contains no rule enforcement at all, so LifecycleRules keeps a single allocation; a store method rejects only what it structurally cannot do. save() is the sole writer of both the scalar columns and the JSON blob, which is what keeps them from drifting.
invariants: No store method ever rejects a write for a policy reason -- that is LifecycleRules' job
save() is the only writer of the scalar columns and `data`, which is what prevents projection drift
Edge and commit inserts are idempotent via table constraints, not application checks

The active-task state is a single in-memory pointer per scope, NOT persisted and does NOT survive a restart (task:f5ace343) -- replaced the durable per-scope LIFO stack (ACTIVE_TASK_STACK, itself a replacement for the older single-row ACTIVE_TASK table, task:f302eb2b). ACTIVE_TASK_STACK is dropped from schema.TABLES but its Table()/index constant stays defined per the additive-only migration rule, so pre-existing rows are left in place, orphaned.
FTS5 absence degrades search rather than failing at import
_combination_score scores tags and body against DISJOINT word sets -- a word counted as a tag match is excluded from the body-overlap count, so it can never score twice
taskstore-data-access-only.name: taskstore-data-access-only

taskstore-round-trip-and-relational-guar.description: Protects TaskStore's round-trip fidelity (every Task field, including nested ResolutionItem and grooming dict content, survives save/get unchanged) and its relational guarantees for edges: link() is idempotent, edges() reports both incoming and outgoing directions, and unlink() -- added specifically because its absence in the prior system left stale edges with no way to clear -- removes either a specific relation or all relations between two tasks and reports the exact count removed.
invariants: save() followed by get() returns a Task equal in every field to what was saved, including resolution item done-state and nested grooming/tags/files structures.
save() is an upsert keyed on id -- saving the same id twice updates the one row rather than creating a second.
link(a, b, rel) returns True on first creation and False on a no-op repeat; edges(a)['outgoing'] and edges(b)['incoming'] both reflect the same link.
unlink(a, b, rel) removes only that relation and returns the count removed; unlink(a, b) with no rel removes all relations between the pair.
Task.progress is always computed from resolution at access time -- mutating a fetched Task's resolution list changes .progress with no explicit resync step.
taskstore-round-trip-and-relational-guar.name: taskstore-round-trip-and-relational-guarantees-tested

taskstore-search-degrades-and-ranks-by-t.description: Pins TaskStore.search()'s two non-obvious properties: an invalid FTS5 query (e.g. an unbalanced quote, which is a plausible user typo) must degrade to a usable fallback rather than raising a 500-class error, and a match against a task's tags must rank above a match found only in body text even when title text is otherwise equal, without breaking ranking for queries that don't touch tags at all.
invariants: A malformed FTS5 query string never raises out of search() -- it falls back to a broader match strategy instead.
search() results reflect the current row state, not a stale index -- updating a task's title makes old-title queries stop matching and new-title queries start matching immediately.
When a query term matches one task's tags and another task's body only, the tag match ranks first, but this weighting must not change relative ranking for queries that match neither task's tags.
taskstore-search-degrades-and-ranks-by-t.name: taskstore-search-degrades-and-ranks-by-tag

tool-called-refusal-vs-exception-semanti.description: Pins tool_called's exact gating rule: its post hook and its OK/REFUSE/ERROR log line are both keyed on the absence of an 'error' key in call.result, never on a truthy 'ok' key or on the result being a dict at all. This lets read tools (no 'ok' key) and list tools (bare list, no key to write a marker into) compose uniformly with write tools under the same hook.
invariants: post runs exactly when call.result is a dict without an 'error' key; it never runs on a dict with 'error', a non-dict result, or when the wrapped block raises.
Logging (OK/REFUSE rule=/ERROR) is unconditional and independent of whether post/pre hooks are supplied -- it must fire even with zero hooks configured.
A raised exception inside the with-block always re-raises after being logged; post is never invoked in that case.
tool-called-refusal-vs-exception-semanti.name: tool-called-refusal-vs-exception-semantics

contracts: Task.to_dict()/to_json() and Task.from_dict()/from_json() round-trip every field
Task.progress -> (done, total), derived from resolution on every read
Task.search_text() flattens the fields worth indexing

TASK_EDGE_RELATIONS is the closed vocabulary for task_edges.rel (10 relations: depends_on, blocks, relates_to, duplicates, removes, implements, supersedes, reverts, writes_to, extends), enforced by lifecycle.check_link_rel on tasks__link. Confirmed against real usage in task_edges before being formalised (task:1c9d37d7) — 4 trace to Jira's issue-link-type vocabulary, the other 6 are this framework's own emergent vocabulary. parent_of was deliberately excluded as redundant with Task.parent.
typed-task-object.description: A task is one typed dataclass serialised to JSON. Two issue types only (epic, task) and four statuses. Typing removes two things outright rather than relocating them: required-section validation becomes schema validation, and 'resolution must be a checklist' becomes unrepresentable because resolution IS a list of items.
invariants: A grooming risk carries a stable, framework-assigned `id` (task:f24be6e4) — assigned by tasks__update whenever an incoming risk lacks one, never accepted from the caller, so no caller can collide with an existing id.

grooming.risks is the one field on Task.grooming that does not replace wholesale: tasks__update._merge_grooming_risks unions current and incoming risks by id, so a re-groom that omits a graded risk carries it forward automatically instead of destroying its grade by omission. Every other grooming field stays wholesale-replace.

A risk written before task:f24be6e4 has no id and is never rewritten to gain one — it is matched to an incoming risk by normalised text on its first post-migration merge, and stays id-less in storage otherwise.
from_dict drops unknown keys rather than raising, so a store written by a newer version stays readable by an older one
progress is never stored — it cannot drift from the list it counts
notes exists deliberately as the escape hatch for anything the schema did not anticipate, and must survive later tidying
Links are never stored in the task blob; they live in task_edges where the primary key makes them idempotent
TASK_EDGE_RELATIONS is enforced only on creation (tasks__link) — removal (tasks__unlink) is deliberately ungated so a legacy or invalid rel value never becomes permanently stuck
typed-task-object.name: typed-task-object

meta.note: Architectural concepts, one or more per module. Ground truth is the code; this is a durable summary of what each module promises and what must stay true of it. The SysML model under models/ is derived FROM this, never the reverse — code -> concepts -> model, one direction only.
